time.desc: A regional economy announced that it would simultaneously suspend its tariff countermeasures against a certain country for about three months in response to the other party's temporary tariff suspension arrangement.

Agency A’s executive order exempts certain commodity categories including copper, pharmaceuticals, semiconductors, wood products, certain critical minerals and energy products
Agency A Confirm that other tariffs imposed on Country X goods by Leader A in the previous term are still effective, and the actual tax rates for some goods are higher.
The market reacted negatively to ultra-high tariffs, with major stock indexes falling sharply
A country's customs department issued rules to grant major tariff exemptions to some core electronic and information products to alleviate price and supply chain impacts.

The leader of a country announced the launch of a trade investigation into the semiconductor and electronics supply chain on the grounds of national security and said that the previous exemption from tariffs on electronic products was only a temporary arrangement.
Country Y Trade chief says critical technology products from Country X will face new separate tariffs over the next two months, with semiconductors to be included

The ruling team A launched a national security investigation into semiconductor and pharmaceutical imports in accordance with relevant regulations and made new progress. Leader A revealed that semiconductor tariff rates will be announced soon.

Country X The top leader embarked on a diplomatic tour Region H and published a signed article, saying that "there are no winners in trade wars and tariff wars" and calling for the maintenance of the multilateral trading system
Leader A said it might temporarily exempt the auto industry from tariffs to give car companies time to move production back home and adjust their supply chains.
Regional Organization A Trade Commissioner reiterates willingness to reach fair agreement on industrial products with "zero-to-zero" tariff plan

Officials from the ruling team A argued that the tariff exemption for some technology products was a "tightrope" strategy between pressuring the manufacturing industry to return and reducing the burden on consumers.
Leader A said he "doesn't blame Country X at all" for causing his country's economic dependence, and praised the other party's top leader as "very smart"

Country Y The head of the monetary authority issued a clear warning on tariff policy for the first time, saying that tariffs are likely to increase inflation at least temporarily and possibly more permanently.
Affected by aggressive tariff policies, investors continued to shift from the U.S. dollar to related currencies, and the currency's exchange rate against Country Y hit a new high for the year.

For the first time, a leader of a country has publicly confirmed that he is in contact and communicating with his counterparty on tariff issues, sending a more obvious signal of negotiation than before.

Leader A said it would not fire Country Y the head of the monetary authority and suggested a tariff regulation could be "significantly reduced" but not completely eliminated, sending stock indexes higher

International agencies downgraded Country Y economic growth forecasts the most among advanced economies and predicted that sharp rises in tariffs would lead to a "significant slowdown" in global growth.

Leader A expects to reach an agreement and finalize tariff figures with Country X within the next two to three weeks, claiming to be in direct contact with the other side's top leaders on a daily basis
The two sides openly disagreed over "whether there are ongoing trade negotiations." The opponent denied it and demanded that unilateral tariff measures be withdrawn first.
City E’s cancellation of import tariffs on some Country Y integrated circuits was not announced publicly and was disclosed to the media by the importer.

The two countries confirmed that they will hold an upgraded high-level face-to-face meeting, and relevant officials publicly acknowledged that the ultra-high tariff situation is unsustainable and will focus on "cooling down"

After the phone call, the leaders of the two countries announced the urgent arrangement of a new round of economic and trade talks to resolve differences on tariffs and the supply of key resources, and released a signal of easing of personnel exchange policies.
